body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **3.0.7** to **3.3.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.3.1
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Added license info to metadata, following PEP-639. Thanks to Gedalia Pasternak and
  Marc Mueller for submitted issue and PR. Fixes 626.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.0
   ```
   ------------------------------
===========================================================================================
 The version 3.3.0 release will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings` for pyparsing methods
 that have been renamed to PEP8-compliant names (introduced in pyparsing 3.0.0, in August,
 2021, with legacy names retained as aliases). In preparation, I added in pyparsing
 3.2.2 a utility for finding and replacing the legacy method names with the new names.
 This utility is located at `pyparsing/tools/cvt_pep8_names.py`. This script will scan all
 Python files specified on the command line, and if the `-u` option is selected, will
 replace all occurrences of the old method names with the new PEP8-compliant names,
 updating the files in place.

 Here is an example that converts all the files in the pyparsing `/examples` directory:

      python -m pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names -u examples/*.py

 The new names are compatible with pyparsing versions 3.0.0 and later.
===========================================================================================

- Deprecated `indentedBlock`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes will be required.
  This is because the new `IndentedBlock` class no longer requires the calling code
  to supply an indent stack, while adding support for nested indentation levels
  and grouping.

- Deprecated `locatedExpr`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes may be required.
  The new `Located` class removes the extra grouping level of the parsed values.
  (If the original `locatedExpr` parser was defined with a results name, then
  the extra grouping is retained, so that the results name nesting works properly;
  in this case, no code changes would be required.)

- Updated all examples and test cases to use PEP8 names (unless the test case is specifically
  designed to test behavior of a legacy method). Added railroad diagrams for some examples.

- Added exception handling when calling `formatted_message()`, so that `str(exception)`
  always returns at least _something_.

- All unit tests pass with Python 3.14, including 3.14t. This does _not_ necessarily
  mean that pyparsing is now thread-safe, just that when run in the free-threaded
  interpreter, there were no errors. None of the unit tests try to do any parsing
  with multiple threads - they test the basic functionality of the library, under various
  versions of packrat and left-recursive parsing.

- Added AI instructions so that AI agents can be prompted with best practices
  for generating parsers using pyparsing code. These instructions are in the
  `ai/best_practices.md` file, and can be accessed programmatically by calling
  `pyparsing.show_best_practices()` or running `python -m pyparsing.ai.show_best_practices`
  from the command line, after installing the `pyparsing` package.

- Implemented a TINY language parser/interpreter using pyparsing, in the `examples/tiny`
  directory. This is a little tutorial language that I used to demonstrate how to use pyparsing to
  build a simple interpreter, following a recommended parser+AST+engine+run structure.
  The `docs` sub-directory also includes transcripts of the AI session used to create the
  parser and the interpreter. The `samples` sub-directory includes a few sample TINY programs.

- Fixed minor formatting bugs in `pyparsing.testing.with_line_numbers`, found during development
  of the TINY language example.

- Added test in `DelimitedList` and `nested_expr` which auto-suppress delimiting commas to
  avoid wrapping in a `Suppress` if delimiter is already a `Suppress`.

- Added performance benchmarking tools and documentation:
  - `tests/perf_pyparsing.py` runs a series of benchmark parsing tests, exercising different
    aspects of the pyparsing package. For cross-version analysis, this script can export
    results as CSV and append to a consolidated data file.
  - Runner scripts `run_perf_all_tags.bat` (Windows) and `run_perf_all_tags.sh` (Ubuntu/bash)
    execute the benchmark across multiple Python versions (3.9–3.14) and pyparsing versions
    (3.1.1 through 3.3.0), aggregating results into `perf_pyparsing.csv` at the repo root.
  - See `tests/README.md` for usage instructions.

- Used performance benchmarking to identify and revert an inefficient utility method used in
  `transform_string` (introduced in pyparsing 3.2.0b2).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.5
   ```
   -------------------------------
- JINX! Well, 3.2.4 had a bug for `Word` expressions that include a space
  character, if that expression was then copied, either directly with .copy() or
  by adding a results name, or included in another construct (like `DelimitedList`)
  that makes a copy internally. Issue 618, reported by mstinberg, among others -
  thanks, and sorry for the inconvenience.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.4
   ```
   -------------------------------
- Barring any catastrophic bugs in this release, this will be the last release in
  the 3.2.x line. The next release, 3.3.0, will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings`

  including available automation for converting any existing code using
  pyparsing with the old names).

- Fixed bug when using a copy of a `Word` expression (either by using the explicit
  `copy()` method, or attaching a results name), and setting a new expression name,

  `Regex` expressions with `as_match` or `as_group_list` = True. Reported by
  Waqas Ilyas, in Issue 612 - good catch!

- Fixed type annotation for `replace_with`, to accept `Any` type. Fixes Issue 602,

- Added locking around potential race condition in `ParserElement.reset_cache`, as

author: bheemreddy-samsara
body:
### Problem

On some apps, harness runs can intermittently fail at startup with a redbox:

> Expected HMRClient.setup() call at startup

Root cause: `@react-native-harness/runtime` schedules `HMRClient.disable()` on a timer, but React Native hasn't always invoked `HMRClient.setup()` yet, so RN throws and the harness never reports ready.

### Fix

- Add `disableHMRWhenReady` helper that retries `disable()` when it fails with the specific RN invariant, then succeeds once setup is complete.
- Keep behavior identical once RN has initialized `HMRClient`.

### Tests

- Add a unit test that simulates the invariant on the first call and verifies we retry and eventually disable successfully.

### Validation

- `pnpm nx test @react-native-harness/runtime`
- `pnpm nx lint @react-native-harness/runtime`
- `pnpm nx typecheck @react-native-harness/runtime`
- `pnpm nx build @react-native-harness/runtime`

This pull request introduces significant improvements to the user experience and data handling in the home and map screens of the Surf Ceylon app. The main focus is on personalizing surf spot recommendations, improving map marker interactivity, and integrating real 7-day forecasts for surf spots. The changes enhance data fetching based on user preferences and location, add loading and refresh states, and provide a more informative and interactive map interface.

**Personalized Recommendations & Data Fetching**
- Home screen now fetches and displays the top three surf spots tailored to the user's preferences and location, replacing static dummy data. Loading and pull-to-refresh states are added for a smoother experience. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-402591ac1893ae954a8e4ac21d92ee1710f9bc5d573ddcdb547f6a86bca551d0L1-R55) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-402591ac1893ae954a8e4ac21d92ee1710f9bc5d573ddcdb547f6a86bca551d0L71-R144)
- The home screen's subtitle and section title are updated to emphasize personalized recommendations.

**Map Screen Enhancements**
- Map markers are now visually differentiated based on selection and surf spot score, with improved styling for clarity and interactivity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bL176-R184) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bR194-R222) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bR399-R403)
- The spot detail panel on the map is now scrollable, supports nested scrolling, and displays additional spot information in a more organized layout. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bR236-R240) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bL399-R451)

**Forecast Integration**
- Both the spot detail screen and the map spot info panel now pass `spotId` to the `ForecastChart` component, enabling it to fetch and display real 7-day forecast data for each spot. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f964d0b2db919577147087c3e3fbd4a4a85a8634ca7d669efdb062cebdcd4f5L321-R322) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-42e5220f195e7de983345a2775247e4072e645f711425f934b43cdb9e254208bR291-R296)

**General UI Improvements**
- The "My Location" button on the map now uses a consistent icon from the Ionicons library.
- Minor style adjustments and new styles are added for chart display and improved layout.

**Feature Navigation**
- The dashboard screen disables navigation for features not yet implemented, logging a message instead of attempting to route.

author: giegiey
body:
## Overview

Addresses issue where mobile app initialization ran twice on startup, causing duplicate notifications and potential race conditions.

## Issues Fixed

1. Connected notification appeared twice on mobile app startup
2. initializeWithConfig() called from two locations simultaneously
3. playcheckNetwork() executed twice due to duplicate initialization
4. Potential race conditions from concurrent app initialization flows
5. No guard mechanism to prevent duplicate initialization

## Technical Changes

1. Added isAppInitialized guard flag to prevent duplicate initialization
2. Modified initializeWithConfig() to check guard flag and return early if already initialized
3. Guard flag set to true on first successful initialization
4. Follows singleton pattern for app initialization lifecycle
5. Matches Electron desktop version's single initialization pattern

## Root Cause

The app had two initialization paths:
- configLoaded event listener at line 251 (when config loads asynchronously)
- Fallback check at line 1119 (checking if config already loaded)

Both paths called initializeWithConfig() leading to duplicate execution of:
- validateActivation()
- startApplication()
- playcheckNetwork()
- Success notification display

## Files Changed Summary

Mobile App:
- mobile/www/index.html - Added isAppInitialized guard flag and duplicate prevention logic in initializeWithConfig()

## Testing

- Verified Connected notification appears only once on startup
- Confirmed no duplicate playcheckNetwork() calls
- Tested both initialization paths (event listener and fallback)
- Ensured app starts correctly without race conditions
- Validated guard flag prevents duplicate initialization
- Console logs show single initialization sequence

body:
## tl;dr

Noticed a small bug in `QAEnv`; added tests to make sure that behavior does not occur again.

## Problem Description

Original implementation incorrectly handles the case where model's answer fails to be extracted (i.e. model response is malformed). This happens most often in base models, but occasionally also instruct-tuned models.

```python
        if model_answer is None:
            # is_correct not declared, resulting in error.
            reward = 0.0
        else:
            is_correct = self.check_correct(model_answer, self.answer)
            reward = 1.0 if is_correct else 0.0
        return TERMINAL_STATE, reward, True, True, {"correct": bool(is_correct)}
```

This behavior was eliminated.

author: hiromaily
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a refactoring to follow Go best practices for context management by removing `context.Context` from struct fields in the `Ethereum` and `Ripple` types.

Closes #49

## Changes

### Core Refactoring
- ✅ **Ethereum struct**: Removed `ctx` field and updated 45+ methods across 10 files
- ✅ **Ripple struct**: Removed `ctx` field and updated 18+ methods across 9 files
- ✅ **Interface updates**: Updated all interface signatures in `api-interface.go` files
- ✅ **Call site updates**: Updated all method call sites to pass context

### Implementation Details

#### Ethereum (`pkg/wallet/api/ethgrp/eth/`)
- Removed `ctx context.Context` field from struct
- Added `ctx context.Context` as the first parameter to all methods
- Updated files:
  - `ethereum.go` - Constructor updated to use context only for initialization
  - `rpc_eth.go` - 13 methods updated
  - `rpc_eth_tx.go` - 6 methods updated (including special handling for `context.WithTimeout`)
  - `rpc_eth_gas.go` - 2 methods updated
  - `rpc_miner.go` - 4 methods updated
  - `rpc_web3.go` - 2 methods updated
  - `rpc_admin.go` - 4 methods updated
  - `rpc_net.go` - 3 methods updated
  - `rpc_personal.go` - 5 methods updated
  - `client.go` - 2 methods updated
  - `balance.go` - 1 method updated
  - `transaction.go` - 5 methods updated

#### Ripple (`pkg/wallet/api/xrpgrp/xrp/`)
- Removed `ctx context.Context` field from struct
- Added `ctx context.Context` as the first parameter to all methods
- Replaced all `context.Background()` calls with `ctx` parameter
- Updated files:
  - `ripple.go` - Constructor updated
  - `rippleapi_tx.go` - 6 methods updated
  - `rippleapi_address.go` - 3 methods updated
  - `rippleapi_account.go` - 1 method updated
  - `public_account.go` - 2 methods updated
  - `public_transaction.go` - 1 method updated
  - `public_server_info.go` - 1 method updated
  - `admin_keygen.go` - 3 methods updated
  - `balance.go` - 2 methods updated
  - `transaction.go` - 1 method updated

#### Service and Command Layers
- Service layer: Updated to use `context.TODO()` for gradual context propagation
- Command layer: Updated to use `context.Background()` at entry points
- Files updated across `pkg/wallet/service/eth/watchsrv/` and `pkg/wallet/service/xrp/`

## Benefits

1. **Proper Context Lifecycle**: Context is now request-scoped rather than persisted in long-lived objects
2. **Thread Safety**: Eliminates potential concurrency issues from shared struct context
3. **Flexibility**: Callers can now provide different contexts for various operations
4. **Go Best Practices**: Follows standard Go idioms and community conventions
5. **No Breaking Logic**: Purely mechanical refactoring with no logic changes

## Testing

✅ **Linting**: `make lint-fix` - 0 issues  
✅ **Build**: `make check-build` - All targets build successfully  
✅ **Tests**: `make gotest` - All tests pass  
✅ **Dependencies**: `make tidy` - Clean

## Migration Notes

This is a **breaking change** for external users of the `Ethereum` and `Ripple` types. All method calls now require passing a `context.Context` as the first parameter.

### Before:
```go
balance, err := eth.GetBalance(address, eth.QuantityTagLatest)
```

### After:
```go
balance, err := eth.GetBalance(ctx, address, eth.QuantityTagLatest)
```

## Review Checklist

- [x] Context removed from struct fields
- [x] All methods accept `ctx context.Context` as first parameter
- [x] All interfaces updated to match
- [x] All call sites updated
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Linting clean
- [x] Build successful
- [x] No logic changes (purely mechanical refactoring)

body:
### Motivation

- Serve task artifacts from a stable storage backend (R2/S3) instead of fragile `/files/...` workspace paths to avoid 404s and long frontend concatenation of workspace paths.
- Persist pipeline outputs under task-scoped prefixes and expose presigned or public download URLs so UI and APIs consume backend-provided links.
- Provide an admin-capable delete flow that can remove task records and optionally purge stored artifacts.
- Keep V1 pipeline lab UI and template framework frozen (guarded) while allowing task-specific UI/template changes.

### Description

- Added R2 storage foundation and helpers in `gateway/app/storage/r2.py` and documentation in `docs/phase0/checklist.md` to presign and upload artifacts when enabled via envs (e.g. `FEATURE_STORAGE_ENABLED`, `R2_*`).
- Implemented storage abstraction and download helpers in `gateway/app/services/artifact_downloads.py` and `gateway/app/services/artifact_storage.py`, and added `gateway/app/services/task_cleanup.py` for record deletion and (best-effort) storage prefix purge.
- Updated pipeline to upload artifacts and persist storage keys (`raw`, `origin.srt`, `mm.srt`, `mm.txt`, `audio`, `capcut_pack.zip`) via `gateway/app/services/steps_v1.py`, and added short redirect download endpoints that 302 to presigned/public URLs: `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/raw`, `/subs_origin`, `/subs_mm`, `/mm_txt`, `/audio_mm`, `/pack` (implemented in `gateway/app/main.py` and task routers).
- Added `DELETE /api/tasks/{task_id}?delete_assets=1` to delete task records and optionally purge storage prefix; adjusted publish handling to prefer `v1` pack redirect and updated frontend templates (`gateway/app/templates/task_workbench.html`, `gateway/app/templates/tasks.html`) to use short endpoints and server-provided URLs instead of concatenating `/files/...`, and documented curl verification in `README.md`.

### Testing

- Ran `python -m compileall gateway >/dev/null` to byte-compile the codebase and validate imports, which completed successfully.
- Executed the frozen-assets guard using the merge-base approach (local `main` fallback) which reported `OK: frozen assets untouched` to ensure `gateway/app/static/ui.html` and `static/templates/**` were not modified.
- Added Phase0 curl checks documented in `README.md` and `docs/phase0/checklist.md` for manual verification (presign smoke test and download endpoint `curl -I` checks); documentation added but those curl checks were not automatically executed as part of this rollout.
- Commit-level checks (compilation + guard) passed on this branch before committing the changes.

├── domain/

### What this PR does

#### Before this PR:

On architectures that don't support CPU hotplug (ARM64), VMs with CPU pinning (`dedicatedCPUPlacement: true`) and `maxSockets` configured crash with a nil pointer dereference panic:

The crash occurs in `AdjustDomainForTopologyAndCPUSet()` when accessing `domain.Spec.VCPUs.VCPU` without checking if `domain.Spec.VCPUs` is nil.

Added nil check before accessing `domain.Spec.VCPUs.VCPU` to prevent the panic. VMs with CPU pinning now start successfully on ARM64 even when `maxSockets` is configured.

Resolves: #62 

## Summary

Documentation updates and theme scaffolder fixes to improve the developer experience for contributors and theme creators.

## Changes

### Documentation
- Added missing command docs: `create-theme`
- Updated `docs/themes.md` with clearer instructions and development workflow
- Added Development section to main README with setup instructions
- Fixed command references and navigation throughout docs

### Theme Scaffolder (`spg create-theme`)
- Fixed package imports (`@simple-photo-gallery/common` instead of `@simple-photo-gallery/common/src/...`)
- Removed monorepo-only TypeScript path mappings from generated themes
- Updated generated theme README with development instructions

### Import Changes
- Switched from source imports (`@simple-photo-gallery/common/src/gallery`) to package entrypoint imports (`@simple-photo-gallery/common`)
- This aligns with the published package structure and works for external users

## Important: Build `common` First

**The `common` package must be built before TypeScript/ESLint can resolve `@simple-photo-gallery/common` imports.** This is because:
- The package exports from `dist/` (not `src/`)
- TypeScript/ESLint need the built declaration files to resolve types
- Added Development section to README with build instructions

After cloning the repo, run:
```bash
yarn install
yarn workspace @simple-photo-gallery/common build
```

This ensures proper type resolution and avoids "Cannot find module" errors.


### Creating and Building Themes Locally
To create and test a theme during development:

#### From the gallery directory
```cd gallery```

#### Create a new theme
```yarn gallery create-theme my-theme```

#### Build a gallery with your theme (using local CLI)
```yarn gallery build --theme ../themes/my-theme -g /path/to/gallery```

This uses the local development CLI (yarn gallery) instead of the published spg command.

author: k1ngst0m
body:
## Why
The current capture implementation performs synchronous fence waits in the application's render thread during `vkQueuePresentKHR`, which can cause frame pacing variance that is perceptible to users in low-latency game streaming scenarios.

## What Changes
- Add dedicated worker thread using timeline semaphores for async GPU synchronization
- Move fence waiting and IPC operations off the render thread
- Add `GOGGLES_CAPTURE_ASYNC` environment variable for runtime toggle (default: enabled)
- Replace per-frame fences with single timeline semaphore per swapchain
- Add `empty()` method to `SPSCQueue` for idiomatic queue checks
- Add `shutdown()` method to `CaptureManager` for proper cleanup in shared library context

## Impact
- Affected specs: `vk-layer-capture`
- Affected code: `src/capture/vk_layer/vk_capture.cpp`, `src/capture/vk_layer/vk_capture.hpp`, `src/util/queues.hpp`

* **New Features**
  * Async capture worker to offload GPU synchronization from the render thread, with runtime toggle (enabled by default)

  * Graceful worker lifecycle and shutdown to improve capture robustness

* **Chores**

## ✅ Implementation Complete: Unified Stream Control & Persistent Streaming State

### Problem Statement
1. ❌ Web frontend had separate "Start Stream" and "Stop Stream" buttons (violates one-tap principle)
2. ❌ Streaming stopped when switching cameras (required manual restart)

### Solution Implemented ✅

#### 1. Unified Toggle Button
- **Removed**: Separate "Stop Stream" button from controls row
- **Enhanced**: Single button that toggles between states with visual feedback
  - 🟢 Green "Start Stream" when stopped
  - 🔴 Red "Stop Stream" when active
- **Placement**: ✅ **Now positioned in the controls row with other buttons**
- **Result**: 50% fewer buttons, clearer UI, follows modern UX patterns

#### 2. Persistent Streaming State
- **Removed**: `location.reload()` call that reset entire page
- **Added**: State preservation logic in `switchCamera()`
  - Remembers if stream was active before switch
  - Automatically resumes streaming with new camera if it was active
  - Updates formats and flashlight button without page reload
- **Result**: Seamless camera switching, no user intervention needed

### Changes Made

**File**: `app/src/main/java/com/ipcam/CameraService.kt`

**Commit 1** (846126a): Initial implementation
- Unified toggle button with dynamic color/text
- Stream state persistence on camera switch

**Commit 2** (Current): Button placement improvement
- Moved toggle button from stream container to controls row
- Added placeholder text when stream is stopped
- Fixed button positioning issue

### UI Layout

**Controls Row**:
```
[Start/Stop Stream] [Refresh] [Switch Camera] [Toggle Flash] [Resolution▼] [Apply]
```

**Stream Container**:
- Shows placeholder text when stopped: "Click 'Start Stream' to begin"
- Shows stream image when active
- Button no longer moves/shifts position

### Testing & Verification

✅ **Build**: Successful - no compilation errors  
✅ **Button Placement**: Fixed - now in controls row with other buttons  
✅ **Toggle Logic**: Verified correct state transitions  
✅ **Stream Persistence**: Verified automatic stream resumption  
✅ **UI Consistency**: Button stays in fixed position

### User Experience Improvements

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Control buttons | 2 | 1 | -50% UI clutter |
| Clicks to switch camera while streaming | 4 | 2 | -50% interactions |
| Page reloads | 1 per switch | 0 | Instant feedback |
| Button position | Shifts/moves | Fixed | Consistent layout |
| State preservation | ❌ | ✅ | Seamless UX |

## Summary

This PR fixes Content Security Policy (CSP) errors that were preventing JustCall widgets from loading properly in the OpenAI Apps SDK. The fix adds proper CSP configuration and widget metadata to the call tools.

## Changes

- **Added CSP configuration** to `list_calls` and `get_call` tools:
  - `connect_domains`: Allows connections to `https://app.justcall.io`
  - `resource_domains`: Allows loading resources from `https://cdn.justcall.io`

- **Added widget metadata**:
  - `widgetDomain`: Set to `https://mcp.justcall.host`
  - `widgetDescription`: Added descriptive text for both widgets

## Technical Details

The CSP configuration is added via the `openai/widgetCSP` metadata field in the tool definitions. This ensures that OpenAI Apps SDK can properly load and display JustCall widgets without CSP violations.

- Bumped version from `1.2.0` to `1.2.1`

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure Tibber live-measurement code selects the correct home when a `HOME_ID` is provided and logs clearly when it cannot be derived automatically.
- Provide an opt-in fallback path to subscribe directly to Tibber websocket live measurements when the normal real-time gate prevents data flow.
- Make configuration discoverable by adding `HOME_ID` to secrets examples and a `TIBBER_LIVE_MEASUREMENTS_FORCE` toggle.

### Description
- Add `resolve_home()` to `lib/tibber_api.py` to prefer `HOME_ID` from configuration and log selection or missing-home errors. 
- Implement an opt-in forced websocket subscription `forced_live_measurements()` that uses `gql`/`WebsocketsTransport` and `tibber.networking.QueryBuilder` when `TIBBER_LIVE_MEASUREMENTS_FORCE=1` is enabled.
- Expose new settings in `lib/constants.py` and update `.env.example`, `.secrets-example`, and `README.md` to document `HOME_ID` and `TIBBER_LIVE_MEASUREMENTS_FORCE` usage.
- Update imports and live-measurement flow to fallback cleanly and log instructions prompting users to define `HOME_ID` in `.secrets` if needed.

### Testing

- All automated tests passed: `5 passed`.

```
curl -XPOST localhost:9644/v1/cloud_storage/automated_recovery -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"cluster_uuid_override": "9cfeb2f5-44b6-4ea9-a98e-6b041c5fa7b1"}'
```

This PR proposes the corresponding change, followed by supporting it in rpk itself. While I added two test cases within rpadmin, I also have a working rpk code locally that uses this commit and confirmed it is sent to the core logic properly.

```
INFO  2025-12-23 16:10:46,577 [shard 0:admi] cluster - cluster_recovery_manager.cc:174 - Using user-provided cluster UUID override for recovery (cluster uuid override: {9cfeb2f5-44b6-4ea9-a98e-6b041c5fa7b1}, cluster name: {nullopt})
```

Seems the current request does have wrong params, `RetentionBytes` and `RetentionMs`, therefore removed them.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **2.4.7** to **3.3.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.3.1
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Added license info to metadata, following PEP-639. Thanks to Gedalia Pasternak and
  Marc Mueller for submitted issue and PR. Fixes 626.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.0
   ```
   ------------------------------
===========================================================================================
 The version 3.3.0 release will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings` for pyparsing methods
 that have been renamed to PEP8-compliant names (introduced in pyparsing 3.0.0, in August,
 2021, with legacy names retained as aliases). In preparation, I added in pyparsing
 3.2.2 a utility for finding and replacing the legacy method names with the new names.
 This utility is located at `pyparsing/tools/cvt_pep8_names.py`. This script will scan all
 Python files specified on the command line, and if the `-u` option is selected, will
 replace all occurrences of the old method names with the new PEP8-compliant names,
 updating the files in place.

 Here is an example that converts all the files in the pyparsing `/examples` directory:

      python -m pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names -u examples/*.py

 The new names are compatible with pyparsing versions 3.0.0 and later.
===========================================================================================

- Deprecated `indentedBlock`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes will be required.
  This is because the new `IndentedBlock` class no longer requires the calling code
  to supply an indent stack, while adding support for nested indentation levels
  and grouping.

- Deprecated `locatedExpr`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes may be required.
  The new `Located` class removes the extra grouping level of the parsed values.
  (If the original `locatedExpr` parser was defined with a results name, then
  the extra grouping is retained, so that the results name nesting works properly;
  in this case, no code changes would be required.)

- Updated all examples and test cases to use PEP8 names (unless the test case is specifically
  designed to test behavior of a legacy method). Added railroad diagrams for some examples.

- Added exception handling when calling `formatted_message()`, so that `str(exception)`
  always returns at least _something_.

- All unit tests pass with Python 3.14, including 3.14t. This does _not_ necessarily
  mean that pyparsing is now thread-safe, just that when run in the free-threaded
  interpreter, there were no errors. None of the unit tests try to do any parsing
  with multiple threads - they test the basic functionality of the library, under various
  versions of packrat and left-recursive parsing.

- Added AI instructions so that AI agents can be prompted with best practices
  for generating parsers using pyparsing code. These instructions are in the
  `ai/best_practices.md` file, and can be accessed programmatically by calling
  `pyparsing.show_best_practices()` or running `python -m pyparsing.ai.show_best_practices`
  from the command line, after installing the `pyparsing` package.

- Implemented a TINY language parser/interpreter using pyparsing, in the `examples/tiny`
  directory. This is a little tutorial language that I used to demonstrate how to use pyparsing to
  build a simple interpreter, following a recommended parser+AST+engine+run structure.
  The `docs` sub-directory also includes transcripts of the AI session used to create the
  parser and the interpreter. The `samples` sub-directory includes a few sample TINY programs.

- Fixed minor formatting bugs in `pyparsing.testing.with_line_numbers`, found during development
  of the TINY language example.

- Added test in `DelimitedList` and `nested_expr` which auto-suppress delimiting commas to
  avoid wrapping in a `Suppress` if delimiter is already a `Suppress`.

- Added performance benchmarking tools and documentation:
  - `tests/perf_pyparsing.py` runs a series of benchmark parsing tests, exercising different
    aspects of the pyparsing package. For cross-version analysis, this script can export
    results as CSV and append to a consolidated data file.
  - Runner scripts `run_perf_all_tags.bat` (Windows) and `run_perf_all_tags.sh` (Ubuntu/bash)
    execute the benchmark across multiple Python versions (3.9–3.14) and pyparsing versions
    (3.1.1 through 3.3.0), aggregating results into `perf_pyparsing.csv` at the repo root.
  - See `tests/README.md` for usage instructions.

- Used performance benchmarking to identify and revert an inefficient utility method used in
  `transform_string` (introduced in pyparsing 3.2.0b2).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.5
   ```
   -------------------------------
- JINX! Well, 3.2.4 had a bug for `Word` expressions that include a space
  character, if that expression was then copied, either directly with .copy() or
  by adding a results name, or included in another construct (like `DelimitedList`)
  that makes a copy internally. Issue 618, reported by mstinberg, among others -
  thanks, and sorry for the inconvenience.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.4
   ```
   -------------------------------
- Barring any catastrophic bugs in this release, this will be the last release in
  the 3.2.x line. The next release, 3.3.0, will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings`
  when the pre-PEP8 methods are used (see header notes above for more information,
  including available automation for converting any existing code using
  pyparsing with the old names).

- Fixed bug when using a copy of a `Word` expression (either by using the explicit
  `copy()` method, or attaching a results name), and setting a new expression name,
  a raised `ParseException` still used the original expression name. Also affected
  `Regex` expressions with `as_match` or `as_group_list` = True. Reported by
  Waqas Ilyas, in Issue 612 - good catch!

- Fixed type annotation for `replace_with`, to accept `Any` type. Fixes Issue 602,
  reported by esquonk.

- Added locking around potential race condition in `ParserElement.reset_cache`, as
  well as other cache-related methods. Fixes Issue 604, reported by CarlosDescalziIM.

- Substantial update to docstrings and doc generation in preparation for 3.3.0,
  great effort by FeRD, thanks!

- Notable addition by FeRD to convert docstring examples to work with doctest! This
  was long overdue, thanks so much!
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.3
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Fixed bug released in 3.2.2 in which `nested_expr` could overwrite parse actions
  for defined content, and could truncate list of items within a nested list.
  Fixes Issue 600, reported by hoxbro and luisglft, with helpful diag logs and
  repro code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.2
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Released `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names.py` conversion utility to upgrade pyparsing-based
  programs and libraries that use legacy camelCase names to use the new PEP8-compliant
  snake_case method names. The converter can also be imported into other scripts as

        from pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names import pep8_converter

- Fixed bug in `nested_expr` where nested contents were stripped of whitespace when
  the default whitespace characters were cleared (raised in this StackOverflow
  question https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79327649 by Ben Alan). Also addressed
  bug in resolving PEP8 compliant argument name and legacy argument name.

- Fixed bug in `rest_of_line` and the underlying `Regex` class, in which matching a
  pattern that could match an empty string (such as `".*"` or `"[A-Z]*"` would not raise
  a `ParseException` at or beyond the end of the input string. This could cause an
  infinite parsing loop whe

The tool now reads and incorporates repository-specific commit message guidelines (from `CONTRIBUTING.md`, Copilot instructions, and `.gitmessage`) into the AI prompt, ensuring generated messages follow project conventions.

- **Copilot support**: Added support for reading `copilot-instructions.md` from `.github/`, root directory, and as hidden file (`.copilot-instructions.md`)

```markdown
## Commit Message Format
Types: feat, fix, docs
Keep subject under 50 characters

IMPORTANT: Follow these repository-specific commit message guidelines:

author: sperlingxx
body:
Closes #14046

This PR enables the efficient `Table.merge` path for **all types** in out-of-core sort merge operations. Previously, nested types in key or ride-along columns would trigger a fallback to `Table.concatenate` + `orderBy`, which is slower.

### Performance Impact

The `Table.merge` operation is more efficient than `Table.concatenate` + `orderBy` because:
- Merge takes advantage of the fact that input batches are already sorted
- Concatenate + orderBy must re-sort all data from scratch

This optimization now applies to all data types including:
- Nested types in sort key columns (Struct, Array)
- Deeply nested ride-along columns (Array of Struct, Struct with Array/Map, etc.)

### Testing

Added comprehensive tests in `sort_test.py` to verify cuDF merge works correctly with:
1. **Single-level nested key columns** - Array, Struct, Struct of Struct as sort keys
2. **Multi-level nested ride-along columns** - Array of Struct, Array of Array, Array of Map, Struct with Array/Map fields

body:
Cross-platform VPN client (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS) powered by Xray-core, restricted to `persiangames.online` domain for connections and subscriptions.

## Architecture

- **UI Layer**: Flutter app with large connect circle, elapsed time display, routing rules editor
- **Core Layer**: Go wrapper around Xray-core
  - Mobile: gomobile bindings (AAR/xcframework)
  - Desktop: FFI-loaded shared library
- **Platform VPN**: Android `VpnService`, iOS `NEPacketTunnelProvider`

## Domain Validation

Subscription URLs must match exactly `persiangames.online`. Connection links (vmess://, vless://, trojan://, ss://) accept exact match or subdomains (*.persiangames.online):

```dart
// Subscription - exact match only
isAllowedSubscriptionUrl('https://persiangames.online/sub', 'persiangames.online') // ✓
isAllowedSubscriptionUrl('https://cdn.persiangames.online/sub', 'persiangames.online') // ✗

// Connection links - subdomains allowed
validateLink('vless://uuid@server.persiangames.online:443', 'persiangames.online') // ✓
validateLink('vless://uuid@badhost.com:443', 'persiangames.online') // ✗
```

## Key Components

- **Flutter App** (`mobile/flutter_app/`)
  - `main.dart`: Connect UI, state management (Provider), subscription refresh
  - `validators.dart`: Domain validation for VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks
  - `settings_screen.dart`: Routing rules editor, battery options (idle disconnect, low power mode)
  - `subscription_service.dart`: HTTP fetch, periodic refresh (6h via WorkManager/BGAppRefreshTask)

- **Go Core** (`core/go/`)
  - `xray_controller.go`: Start/stop controller (Xray runtime integration pending)
  - `go.mod`: Xray-core v1.8.11 dependency

- **Platform Skeletons**
  - `android/...XrayVpnService.kt`: VPN service with TUN setup
  - `ios/...PacketTunnelProvider.swift`: Network extension with tunnel settings

## Battery Optimization

Settings UI toggles for idle disconnect and low power mode (reduced keepalives, logging). Stubbed in controllers pending Xray config integration.

## Next Steps

1. Build gomobile bindings and wire to platform VPN services
2. Implement config generation from validated connection links
3. Persist settings via SharedPreferences
4. Complete background refresh schedulers

- `README.md`: Build instructions, architecture
- `docs/STORE_COMPLIANCE.md`: iOS Network Extensions, Android VpnService requirements
- `docs/PRIVACY_POLICY.md`: Template (no data collection by default)
- `docs/POST_SCAFFOLD_CHECKLIST.md`: Phase-by-phase development guide

# GOZAR VPN

Cross-platform VPN client for Android, iOS, Windows, and macOS powered by Xray-core. Supports VLESS, VMess, and other Xray protocols. Includes:
- Large connect circle UI with elapsed time display
- Domain restriction: only accepts connection and subscription links from `persiangames.online`

- Battery-friendly operation

## Platforms & Architecture

- UI Layer: Flutter (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS)
- Core Layer: Go wrapper around Xray-core
  - Mobile: Built via gomobile (`AAR` for Android, `.xcframework` for iOS)
  - Desktop: Shared library loaded via FFI
- iOS: NEPacketTunnelProvider network extension for App Store-compliant VPN
- Android: `VpnService` implementation to route traffic through Xray

## Features

- Protocols: VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks (and more supported by Xray)
- Link acceptance restriction:
  - Subscription links must have host `persiangames.online`
  - Direct connection links (e.g., `vmess://`, `vless://`, `trojan://`, `ss://`) must have server host ending with `persiangames.online`
- Routing rules: editable and saved, applied to Xray config
- Subscription refresh: on app start and every ~6 hours (platform schedulers used)
- Battery minimization: controlled keepalives, reduced logging, no wake-locks, idle disconnect

- iOS: Requires Network Extensions capability (Packet Tunnel). Ensure compliance with Apple App Store Review Guidelines:
  - Legitimate VPN use cases
  - Transparent privacy practices

### Motivation

- Consolidate task completion and deletion actions into a single right-side ellipsis to reduce visual clutter and accidental clicks.
- Prevent layout jitter when labels change by keeping the action tray a fixed width and only transforming the hovered button.
- Improve interaction stability by enlarging the hit area and adding a delayed close to avoid the menu collapsing while moving the pointer.
- Provide an explicit two-step confirmation pattern (`hover` → label change → `click`) so hover alone does not trigger business logic.

### Description

- Replaced the previous inline per-item complete/delete controls with an ellipsis action tray implemented in `components/TaskList.tsx` and introduced `openActionId`, `hoveredAction`, and `actionCloseTimer` to manage menu state and delayed close behavior.
- Implemented a fixed-width action tray (`w-[168px]`) containing two buttons that swap to confirmation labels (`已完成？` / `删除？` / `恢复？`) only while hovered, and dim the non-hovered button to avoid layout shifts.
- Added an expanded hit area and a 160ms delayed close (`scheduleCloseActionMenu`) plus cleanup in a `useEffect` to maintain a stable hover → move → click flow without accidental collapse.
- Removed the old single-button hover implementation and adjusted imports accordingly (`Check`/`Trash2` icons removed) and wired clicks to only act when in the confirmation state (`handleConfirmComplete` / `archiveTask` / `toggleDone`).

### Testing

- Ran `npm run dev` to start the Next.js dev server and the app compiled, but runtime SSR failed with a `FirebaseError: auth/invalid-api-key` preventing a full end-to-end verification. (failed)
- Attempted a browser smoke check via Playwright to capture a screenshot of the new UI, but the tool could not reach the local server (`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`), so the visual test did not complete. (failed)
- No unit or integration test suite was executed as part of this change. (not run)
- The change was linted/compiled as part of development start and committed locally. (partial success)

author: amoisis
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/amoisis/volkswagen_goconnect/security/code-scanning/2](https://github.com/amoisis/volkswagen_goconnect/security/code-scanning/2)

In general, the fix is to ensure that sensitive information (passwords, tokens, etc.) is never written to logs. The simplest way here is to avoid logging the full `data` payload when it may contain credentials and instead log a redacted or filtered version that omits or masks sensitive fields, while still logging non-sensitive information for debugging.

The best targeted fix without changing existing functionality is to modify `_api_wrapper` in `custom_components/volkswagen_goconnect/api.py` so that it does not log `data` directly. Instead, create a sanitized copy (e.g., `safe_data`) where known sensitive keys such as `"password"` (and optionally `"deviceToken"` or `"Authorization"` if they could ever appear in `data`) are replaced with a fixed mask like `"***REDACTED***"`. Then log `safe_data`. This way, authentication still works exactly the same, but sensitive values are not exposed in logs. No changes are required in `config_flow.py` beyond this, because only the logging of `data` is problematic; passing the password into the API client is expected.

Concretely:
- Edit `VolkswagenGoConnectApiClient._api_wrapper` in `custom_components/volkswagen_goconnect/api.py`.
- Replace the single `_LOGGER.debug("Data: %s", data)` line with logic that constructs a redacted copy and logs that instead.
- No new imports are needed: a shallow `dict` copy and simple looping suffice.

This single change addresses all reported variants because they all flow into the same logging sink (`_LOGGER.debug("Data: %s", data)`).

body:
## Summary

  Implements a comprehensive subscription management system with email notifications, plan-based access controls, and Stripe webhook integration for handling plan upgrades/downgrades.

  ## Features Added

  ### 📧 Email Notification System
  - **Templates**: Welcome, plan upgraded, grace period started, and access restricted emails
  - **Delivery**: Resend integration with webhook confirmation tracking
  - **Automation**:
    - Automatic welcome email on user signup (Better Auth onCreate trigger)
    - Plan upgrade/downgrade notifications
    - Daily cron job for access restriction emails (03:00 UTC)

  ### 💳 Billing & Webhooks
  - **Stripe Integration**: HMAC-SHA256 webhook signature verification
  - **Event Handling**: Subscription created, updated, deleted, and payment failed
  - **Idempotency**: In-memory cache to prevent duplicate event processing

  ### 🔒 Access Control & Restrictions
  - **Free Plan Limits**:
    - Restricted to 2 most recent projects
    - 7-day grace period after downgrade
    - Blocked access to shared projects when restricted
  - **Pro Plan Features**:
    - Unlimited projects
    - Project sharing with quota tracking (`project_shares` feature)
    - Pro-only feature gating (`can_share_project`)

  ### 🚀 Project Sharing Enhancements
  - **Pro Plan Gating**: Requires Pro plan to share projects
  - **Usage Tracking**: Autumn integration for share quota (+1 on create, -1 on revoke)
  - **Limit Enforcement**: `PROJECT_SHARES_LIMIT_REACHED` error when quota exceeded

  ### 🛡️ Security & Rate Limiting
  - **Rate Limit Fix**: Moved rate limit checks before external service calls (Autumn)
  - **Error Handling**: Added `PRO_PLAN_REQUIRED` and `PROJECT_SHARES_LIMIT_REACHED` error codes

  ## Technical Changes

  ### Modified Files
  - `convex/auth.ts` - Added onCreate trigger for welcome emails
  - `convex/user.ts` - Email handlers and plan management
  - `convex/betterAuth/user.ts` - Email tracking and grace period queries
  - `convex/project.ts` - Rate limiting fixes
  - `convex/projectShare.ts` - Converted to actions, added Pro gating and tracking
  - `convex/lib/access.ts` - Implemented project restrictions for free users
  - `convex/lib/errors.ts` - New error codes for sharing and pro plan
  - `convex/http.ts` - Stripe and Resend webhook handlers
  - `convex/crons.ts` - Daily access restriction email cron

  ### New Files
  - `convex/lib/emails/` - Email templates (welcome, grace period, access restricted, plan upgraded)
  - `convex/resend.ts` - Email rendering and delivery
  - `convex/stripe.ts` - Stripe webhook verification

  ### Removed Files
  - `convex/webhook.ts` - Replaced by stripe.ts with proper verification
  - `convex/betterAuth/lib/types.ts` - Consolidated into lib/types.ts

  ## Testing Notes

  ### Email Flow
  1. User signs up → Welcome email sent automatically
  2. User upgrades to Pro → Plan upgraded email sent
  3. User downgrades to Free → Grace period email sent immediately
  4. After 7 days → Access restricted email sent via cron

  ### Access Restrictions
  1. Free user with >2 projects → Only 2 newest accessible
  2. Access-restricted user → Cannot access shared projects
  3. Free user tries to share → `PRO_PLAN_REQUIRED` error
  4. Pro user at share limit → `PROJECT_SHARES_LIMIT_REACHED` error

  ### Webhooks
  - Stripe webhook: `/webhook/stripe` with signature verification
  - Resend webhook: `/webhook/resend` for delivery confirmation

  ## Deployment Requirements

  **Environment Variables** (ensure these are set):
  ```bash
  RESEND_API_KEY=re_xxx
  STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_xxx
  SITE_URL=https://relic.so

  Autumn Features (configure in dashboard):
  - can_share_project (boolean): Free = false, Pro = true
  - project_shares (limit): Free = 0, Pro = 10 (or desired limit)

body:
## Policy Violation Remediation

**Cluster:** remediator-host

**Namespace:** nginx

**File:** apps/nginx/deployment.yaml

## Remediation Results

| Policy Name | Explanation | Runtime Impact | Confidence |
|-------------|-------------|----------------|------------|
| disallow-capabilities | Removed SYS_ADMIN capability as it's not in the baseline allowed capabilities list | Application will lose administrative system capabilities; functionality requiring elevated privileges will fail | low |
| disallow-host-path | Replaced hostPath volume with emptyDir to eliminate host filesystem access | Application loses access to host /etc directory; nginx may fail if it needs host-specific configuration files | low |
| disallow-privilege-escalation | Added allowPrivilegeEscalation: false to container security context | Container cannot escalate privileges during runtime; most applications work fine with this restriction | high |
| restrict-seccomp-strict | Added seccompProfile with type RuntimeDefault to both pod and container security contexts | Application syscalls will be restricted to default profile; most applications work fine with RuntimeDefault | high |
| disallow-privileged-containers | Changed privileged: true to privileged: false to disable privileged mode | Container loses all privileged access to host; applications requiring kernel-level access will fail | low |
| disallow-capabilities-strict | Removed SYS_ADMIN capability and added 'drop: ALL' to comply with strict capability restrictions | Application will lose administrative privileges; if nginx requires system-level operations, it will fail to function properly | low |
| require-run-as-nonroot | Added runAsNonRoot: true to pod security context to ensure containers run as non-root user | Nginx will attempt to run as non-root user; default nginx image runs as root, so container will likely fail to start | low |
| disallow-host-ports | Removed hostPort: 80 from container port configuration to disable host port binding | Service will no longer be accessible directly on host port 80; requires Service/Ingress for external access | high |
| restrict-volume-types | Replaced hostPath volume with emptyDir to use only allowed volume types | Application will lose access to host /etc directory; if nginx configuration depends on host files, it will fail | low |
| restrict-automount-sa-token | Added automountServiceAccountToken: false to disable automatic service account token mounting | Pod cannot access Kubernetes API using mounted service account; API-dependent features will fail | high |

author: copilot
body:
Build a Unity-based third-person arena survival game featuring player combat mechanics, three enemy AI types, and progressive wave spawning in a procedurally generated circular stone arena.

## Implementation

**Core Player Systems** (`PlayerController.cs`, `CameraController.cs`)
- Third-person movement with CharacterController and camera-relative input
- Dodge roll with invulnerability frames (0.5s) and stamina cost (25 SP)
- Dual melee attacks: light (15 dmg, 10 SP, 0.5s CD) and heavy (35 dmg, 30 SP, 1.5s CD)
- Stamina regeneration (15 SP/sec) with action-blocking when depleted

**Enemy AI System** (`EnemyController.cs`, `Projectile.cs`)
- NavMesh pathfinding with three distinct behaviors:
  - **Rusher**: Direct pursuit (6 speed, 30 HP, 8 melee damage)
  - **Brute**: Slow tank (2 speed, 100 HP, 25 melee damage, 1.5x scale)
  - **Caster**: Kiting ranged (3 speed, 20 HP, 12 projectile damage, maintains 8 unit distance)
- Attack cooldowns and range-based engagement

**Wave Management** (`WaveSpawner.cs`, `GameManager.cs`)
- Progressive difficulty scaling (1.2x multiplier per wave, 20 enemy cap)
- Weighted enemy distribution (50% Rusher, 30% Brute, 20% Caster)
- Circular perimeter spawning with 10s rest periods

**Environment** (`ArenaBuilder.cs`, `TorchFlicker.cs`)
- Procedural 15-radius circular arena with 5-height walls
- 8 cylindrical pillars for cover (0.8 radius, 4 height, 10 units from center)
- 12 flickering torches with Perlin noise intensity variation
- Exponential fog (0.02 density) and low ambient lighting (0.2 RGB)

**UI & Utilities** (`GameUIController.cs`, `GameSceneSetup.cs`)
- Health/stamina bars, survival timer, wave counter, game over screen
- Auto-setup script for rapid scene configuration
- Debug visualizer for development

## Example Usage

```csharp
// Enemy type configuration in EnemyController
void ConfigureEnemyType() {
    switch (enemyType) {
        case EnemyType.Rusher:
            moveSpeed = 6f; maxHealth = 30f; attackDamage = 8f;
            break;
        case EnemyType.Brute:
            moveSpeed = 2f; maxHealth = 100f; attackDamage = 25f;
            transform.localScale = new Vector3(1.5f, 1.5f, 1.5f);
            break;
        case EnemyType.Caster:
            moveSpeed = 3f; maxHealth = 20f; attackDamage = 12f;
            attackRange = 8f; // Maintains distance
            break;
    }
}
```

## Project Structure
- 11 C# scripts (1,450 lines)
- Unity 2022.3.10f1 scene with lighting configuration
- Documentation: README, quickstart guide, technical docs, build instructions

author: mrxana91
body:
This PR adds a scroll wrap around capability to the `MenuLayer` ui object, alongside some vibe functionalities.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89f6ddad-ab90-4c5d-8b58-78cda4a9a180

## New behaviors
### Scroll wrap-around
Pressing the 'up' button when the first element of the `MenuLayer` is selected will wrap around and bring the cursor to the last element.
Pressing the 'down' button when the last element of the `MenuLayer` is selected will wrap around and bring the cursor to the first element.
However, wrap around will not be applied when holding down the 'up' or 'down' button, and cursor will still lock on the first or last element.

This wrap-around functionality is disabled by default but can be enabled with the `menu_layer_set_scroll_wrap_around` function.

### Vibe on cursor blocked / vibe on wrap-around
A small 50ms vibe can be activated on wrap-around, or when blocked. Those two behaviors are mutually exclusive (setting one to true will set the other to false).

Those are also disabled by default, but can be enabled using the `menu_layer_set_vibe_on_wrap` and `menu_layer_set_vibe_on_blocked` functions.

## Menu prefs
This PR also implements some new prefs to enable those new capabilties on every `MenuLayer` used accross the firmware system apps. No UI to change those prefs have been implemented in this PR though.

author: armensl
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and improvements to the GUI metamodel, backend API testing, and React code generation. The main focus is on extending the expressiveness of dashboard components (especially charts), improving button action handling and serialization, expanding backend testing documentation, and supporting more granular table features in the React generator.

### GUI Metamodel Enhancements

* Added a new `Series` class to represent data series in charts, and extended the `Chart` class to support multiple data series with appropriate property accessors. This allows for more flexible and complex chart configurations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5d56df5c9baa72b94f7e2b01e7ebb619fcab96842854656801b7539bfc7dbd8aR47-R84) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5d56df5c9baa72b94f7e2b01e7ebb619fcab96842854656801b7539bfc7dbd8aR104-R115)
* Extended the `Button` class to support richer action types (CRUD, navigation, method execution), additional properties (such as `entity_class`, `instance_source`, `is_instance_method`, and confirmation dialog options), and added legacy compatibility for older parameter names. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-52ab7935588677f96ae8b9bd33369ee71dda51c311a72c01a0a7cea43c900ef1R51-L59) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-52ab7935588677f96ae8b9bd33369ee71dda51c311a72c01a0a7cea43c900ef1R711-R756) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-52ab7935588677f96ae8b9bd33369ee71dda51c311a72c01a0a7cea43c900ef1R793-R862)

### Backend and API Testing

* Added a comprehensive `API_METHODS_TESTS.md` guide with example `curl` and `Invoke-WebRequest` commands for testing all generated method endpoints for `Book` and `Library` entities. This includes expected responses and tips for creating test data.

### React Generator Improvements

* Enhanced the serialization logic for buttons to support new method execution features: now, the generator extracts method/class names, endpoint URLs, instance method flags, and input parameters from the `method_btn` property, enabling more robust and dynamic frontend integration.
* Added support for per-column filtering and sorting in tables by including new template files (`ColumnFilter.tsx.j2`, `ColumnSort.tsx.j2`) in the table component generation.

### Miscellaneous

* Updated the Pydantic classes template to import the `time` type, broadening the range of supported field types in generated models.

These changes collectively improve the flexibility, maintainability, and testability of both the backend and frontend codebases, and lay the groundwork for more advanced UI and API features.

author: duau-odoo
body:
Since [1], overlays are no longer visible after an operation that
executes `reloadEditor`.

Steps to reproduce:
- On website, go into edit mode
- Change header template
- After reload, overlays are missing

Reason:
`WebsiteBuilderClientAction.reloadEditor` sets up the new `Editor`
before the old one is destroyed.
Consequently, `LocalOverlayPlugin.destroy` removes the newest overlays
as well. This commit ensures the plugin only cleans up its specific DOM
elements.

The order of operations bug will be fixed in a later PR.

body:
This pull request refactors and streamlines validation logic across several custom validator classes, primarily by centralizing error handling and validator invocation through a new `validate_with` helper method. This results in less repetitive code, improved maintainability, and more consistent error propagation. Additionally, it standardizes the handling of unknown values for action names by introducing and using shared constants.

Key changes include:

**Validation Logic Refactoring:**

* Replaced repetitive validator calls and manual error propagation in `CustomValidator.py` (for `codeql-analysis`, `compress-images`, and `docker-build`) with calls to a new `validate_with` helper method, significantly reducing boilerplate and improving code clarity. **Standardization and Constants:**

* Introduced a shared `DEFAULT_UNKNOWN` constant in `_tests/shared/validation_core.py` and used it consistently for unknown action names in both test and core validation modules, ensuring uniform handling of missing or unknown values. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c41c53ac287d6075f9552d1df839d0f060316f23e4986550d4bd9755440a482R28-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c41c53ac287d6075f9552d1df839d0f060316f23e4986550d4bd9755440a482L500-R505) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d4482bac484f0748f80c479d962327de309188884bc9af2db94615681b024aa7R24-R26) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d4482bac484f0748f80c479d962327de309188884bc9af2db94615681b024aa7L333-R345)

author: katodo
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a way to publish grid cell (slot) selection events to an MQTT broker to automate drawer insert/retrieve flows.
- Allow configuring MQTT connection and which fields are published (cabinet, row/col, items, etc.) via the admin UI.
- Keep the MQTT client optional at runtime so the app still runs when the MQTT dependency is unavailable.

### Description
- Added `MqttSettings` model and default MQTT constants and a `get_mqtt_settings()` helper to store broker and publishing options.
- Implemented `mqtt_payload_for_slot(...)` to build a configurable JSON payload and `publish_mqtt_payload(...)` which performs a dynamic `paho.mqtt.publish.single` call.
- Exposed admin UI controls in `templates/admin/config.html` and a POST route `@app.route('/admin/mqtt/update')` to edit/save MQTT settings, plus a `/admin/mqtt/publish_slot` endpoint to trigger a publish for a specific cabinet/col/row.
- Wired client-side JS (`publishSlotMqtt`) in `templates/index.html` to POST slot click info to the new publish endpoint when a grid cell is selected, and added `paho-mqtt` to `requirements.txt` while keeping the import inside the publish function to avoid import-time failures.

### Testing
- Started the development server with `python magazzino.py` and confirmed `GET /login` returned `200 OK` using `curl`; this validated the app boots with the new changes.
- Attempted automated UI capture with Playwright (login + visit `/admin/config`) but the script failed to connect to the running app (connection refused) during the first attempt and again later.
- Ran `pip install -r requirements.txt` which failed to fetch `paho-mqtt==2.1.0` due to network/proxy errors, so the MQTT library was not installed in this environment (the code imports `paho.mqtt` dynamically inside the publish function to avoid breaking startup).
- Initialized the DB via `init_db()` and launched the app programmatically (`python -c "from magazzino import app, init_db; init_db(); app.run(...)"`) to exercise startup and routing; server started successfully.

### Motivation
- Prevent presigned storage URLs from being rendered into the DOM by ensuring front-end always uses short `/v1/tasks/*` links (server may 302 to presigned URLs). 
- Make the Task Board per-row Delete action stable and use event delegation to avoid fragile per-row handlers. 
- Provide an in-browser compare/copy/edit UI for origin/mm subtitles and let dubbing prefer edited subtitles when present. 
- Keep changes minimal and avoid touching `/tasks/new` or URL parsing logic and the existing PR-4 short-link server behavior.

author: yaziza
body:
Fixed a critical bug in BotanBlockCipher.addBufferedInput() where:

1. Arrays.copyOfRange was copying from inputOffset to input.length instead of copying only inputLen bytes
2. System.arraycopy was using 'index' (inputLen + payload_buffer.length) instead of 'inputLen' as the copy length

This caused ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when:
- payload_buffer had buffered data from a prior update() call
- doFinal() or update() was called with an input array using offset and length
- The condition: (inputLen + payload_buffer.length) > (input.length - inputOffset)

The fix ensures only inputLen bytes are copied from the specified offset.

Added comprehensive tests that verify the fix for both update() and doFinal() methods with various offset/length combinations.

## Summary
- Fix migrate.sh to prioritize individual DATABASE_* environment variables over DATABASE_URL when DATABASE_HOST is explicitly set

## Problem
The migration script was using `DATABASE_URL` which contained `postgres` as hostname (Docker network alias), while `DATABASE_HOST` was correctly set to the external database host. This caused connection failures.

## Solution
When `DATABASE_HOST` is explicitly set (not `localhost`), use individual `DATABASE_*` variables instead of `DATABASE_URL`.

author: evverx
body:
Up until this point avahi-daemon was run under Valgrind on Ubuntu only because the output of Valgrind and its exit code were tracked only there.

On FreeBSD and Alpine the output of Valgrind is forwarded to /dev/null by default (because of libdaemon forwarding stderr there in daemon_fork) so Valgrind is run with --log-file instead and all the errors are looked for there. The suppression file is added to suppress reports where Valgrind complains about 4 file descriptors handled by libdaemon: stdin, stdout, stderr and the syslog socket. It's needed on Ubuntu too but Valgrind isn't new enough on Ubuntu 24.04 on the CI upstream so it doesn't fail with --track-fds=yes yet (even though it complains about the syslog fd).

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **2.4.7** to **3.3.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.3.1
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Added license info to metadata, following PEP-639. Thanks to Gedalia Pasternak and
  Marc Mueller for submitted issue and PR. Fixes 626.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.3.0
   ```
   ------------------------------
===========================================================================================
 The version 3.3.0 release will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings` for pyparsing methods
 that have been renamed to PEP8-compliant names (introduced in pyparsing 3.0.0, in August,
 2021, with legacy names retained as aliases). In preparation, I added in pyparsing
 3.2.2 a utility for finding and replacing the legacy method names with the new names.
 This utility is located at `pyparsing/tools/cvt_pep8_names.py`. This script will scan all
 Python files specified on the command line, and if the `-u` option is selected, will
 replace all occurrences of the old method names with the new PEP8-compliant names,
 updating the files in place.

 Here is an example that converts all the files in the pyparsing `/examples` directory:

      python -m pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names -u examples/*.py

 The new names are compatible with pyparsing versions 3.0.0 and later.
===========================================================================================

- Deprecated `indentedBlock`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes will be required.
  This is because the new `IndentedBlock` class no longer requires the calling code
  to supply an indent stack, while adding support for nested indentation levels
  and grouping.

- Deprecated `locatedExpr`, when converted using the `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names`
  utility, will emit `UserWarnings` that additional code changes may be required.
  The new `Located` class removes the extra grouping level of the parsed values.
  (If the original `locatedExpr` parser was defined with a results name, then
  the extra grouping is retained, so that the results name nesting works properly;
  in this case, no code changes would be required.)

- Updated all examples and test cases to use PEP8 names (unless the test case is specifically
  designed to test behavior of a legacy method). Added railroad diagrams for some examples.

- Added exception handling when calling `formatted_message()`, so that `str(exception)`
  always returns at least _something_.

- All unit tests pass with Python 3.14, including 3.14t. This does _not_ necessarily
  mean that pyparsing is now thread-safe, just that when run in the free-threaded
  interpreter, there were no errors. None of the unit tests try to do any parsing
  with multiple threads - they test the basic functionality of the library, under various
  versions of packrat and left-recursive parsing.

- Added AI instructions so that AI agents can be prompted with best practices
  for generating parsers using pyparsing code. These instructions are in the
  `ai/best_practices.md` file, and can be accessed programmatically by calling
  `pyparsing.show_best_practices()` or running `python -m pyparsing.ai.show_best_practices`
  from the command line, after installing the `pyparsing` package.

- Implemented a TINY language parser/interpreter using pyparsing, in the `examples/tiny`
  directory. This is a little tutorial language that I used to demonstrate how to use pyparsing to
  build a simple interpreter, following a recommended parser+AST+engine+run structure.
  The `docs` sub-directory also includes transcripts of the AI session used to create the
  parser and the interpreter. The `samples` sub-directory includes a few sample TINY programs.

- Fixed minor formatting bugs in `pyparsing.testing.with_line_numbers`, found during development
  of the TINY language example.

- Added test in `DelimitedList` and `nested_expr` which auto-suppress delimiting commas to
  avoid wrapping in a `Suppress` if delimiter is already a `Suppress`.

- Added performance benchmarking tools and documentation:
  - `tests/perf_pyparsing.py` runs a series of benchmark parsing tests, exercising different
    aspects of the pyparsing package. For cross-version analysis, this script can export
    results as CSV and append to a consolidated data file.
  - Runner scripts `run_perf_all_tags.bat` (Windows) and `run_perf_all_tags.sh` (Ubuntu/bash)
    execute the benchmark across multiple Python versions (3.9–3.14) and pyparsing versions
    (3.1.1 through 3.3.0), aggregating results into `perf_pyparsing.csv` at the repo root.
  - See `tests/README.md` for usage instructions.

- Used performance benchmarking to identify and revert an inefficient utility method used in
  `transform_string` (introduced in pyparsing 3.2.0b2).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.5
   ```
   -------------------------------
- JINX! Well, 3.2.4 had a bug for `Word` expressions that include a space
  character, if that expression was then copied, either directly with .copy() or
  by adding a results name, or included in another construct (like `DelimitedList`)
  that makes a copy internally. Issue 618, reported by mstinberg, among others -
  thanks, and sorry for the inconvenience.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.4
   ```
   -------------------------------
- Barring any catastrophic bugs in this release, this will be the last release in
  the 3.2.x line. The next release, 3.3.0, will begin emitting `DeprecationWarnings`
  when the pre-PEP8 methods are used (see header notes above for more information,
  including available automation for converting any existing code using
  pyparsing with the old names).

- Fixed bug when using a copy of a `Word` expression (either by using the explicit
  `copy()` method, or attaching a results name), and setting a new expression name,
  a raised `ParseException` still used the original expression name. Also affected
  `Regex` expressions with `as_match` or `as_group_list` = True. Reported by
  Waqas Ilyas, in Issue 612 - good catch!

- Fixed type annotation for `replace_with`, to accept `Any` type. Fixes Issue 602,
  reported by esquonk.

- Added locking around potential race condition in `ParserElement.reset_cache`, as
  well as other cache-related methods. Fixes Issue 604, reported by CarlosDescalziIM.

- Substantial update to docstrings and doc generation in preparation for 3.3.0,
  great effort by FeRD, thanks!

- Notable addition by FeRD to convert docstring examples to work with doctest! This
  was long overdue, thanks so much!
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.3
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Fixed bug released in 3.2.2 in which `nested_expr` could overwrite parse actions
  for defined content, and could truncate list of items within a nested list.
  Fixes Issue 600, reported by hoxbro and luisglft, with helpful diag logs and
  repro code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.2
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Released `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names.py` conversion utility to upgrade pyparsing-based
  programs and libraries that use legacy camelCase names to use the new PEP8-compliant
  snake_case method names. The converter can also be imported into other scripts as

        from pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names import pep8_converter

- Fixed bug in `nested_expr` where nested contents were stripped of whitespace when
  the default whitespace characters were cleared (raised in this StackOverflow
  question https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79327649 by Ben Alan). Also addressed
  bug in resolving PEP8 compliant argument name and legacy argument name.

- Fixed bug in `rest_of_line` and the underlying `Regex` class, in which matching a
  pattern that could match an empty string (such as `".*"` or `"[A-Z]*"` would not raise
  a `ParseException` at or beyond the end of the input string. This could cause an

body:
The workflow was failing with "No virtual environment found" when executing `uv pip install coverage pytest`. This occurred because `uv pip install` requires an active virtual environment, but one wasn't guaranteed to exist in all execution paths (e.g., when dependency cache is hit or only requirements.txt is present).

**Changes:**
- Added virtual environment check before installing coverage and pytest
- Creates `.venv` using `uv venv` if it doesn't already exist
- Ensures consistent behavior across Poetry, uv sync, and pip-based dependency workflows

```yaml
- name: Run tests with coverage
  run: |
    mkdir -p test-results coverage-results
    # Ensure virtual environment exists
    if [ ! -d ".venv" ]; then
      uv venv
    fi
    uv pip install coverage pytest
    uv run coverage run -m pytest ...
```

  - Flask route endpoints (/, /api/metadata, /api/ratings, /api/rate)
  - Rating system CRUD operations (create, update, delete)

  - Error handling and input validation

  - Metadata display elements
  - Rating system buttons and counters

### CI/CD Integration
- ✅ GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) that:
  - Runs on every push and pull request to master/main
  - Executes Python and frontend tests in parallel
  - Generates coverage reports for both test suites
  - Posts test results and coverage percentages as PR comments
  - Uploads coverage artifacts (30-day retention)

### Build System & Documentation

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimized code achieves a **6% speedup** through several micro-optimizations that reduce attribute lookups and function calls in the hot path:

## Key Optimizations

1. **Hoisting `ruleset.get` outside the loop** (`ruleset_get = ruleset.get`): This avoids repeated attribute lookups on the dict object during every ruleset check. While the gain per lookup is small, it accumulates across iterations.

2. **Caching `element.metadata` and `top_element.metadata`**: By storing `metadata = element.metadata` and `top_metadata = top_element.metadata`, the code eliminates redundant attribute access. The line profiler shows this saves ~0.5-1.0μs per element in the hot path.

3. **Using empty tuple `()` instead of list `[]` as default**: Changing `ruleset.get(top_element_category, [])` to `ruleset.get(top_element_category, ())` avoids allocating a new list object on each miss. Python tuples are immutable and can be reused, while `[]` creates a fresh object each time.

4. **Restructuring conditional logic**: The optimized version splits the compound condition into separate `if/elif` branches. This allows early exit when `top_element_category == element_category` without evaluating the ruleset lookup, which is more expensive due to the `in` membership test on a list.

## Performance Context

Based on the **function_references**, `set_element_hierarchy()` is called in a decorator (`add_metadata`) that wraps document partitioning functions. This means it runs **once per document** after element extraction, but before final metadata assignment. While not in a tight loop, it processes potentially hundreds to thousands of elements per document, making these micro-optimizations worthwhile.

The **annotated_tests** show the optimization is most effective for:
- **Large hierarchies** with many elements (500-1000 elements): 3-11% faster
- **Deep nested structures**: 4-8% faster

author: st4nni
body:
This feature adds a RDF to ROCrate interoperability module that allows to export ROCrates as RDF graph and import ROCrates from RDF graphs. All conversion is funneled through the `ROCrate` struct.

- Add RDF serialization/deserialization support via new `rdf` feature flag
- Implement bidirectional conversion: ROCrate struct ↔ RDF triples
- Support multiple RDF formats for export and import: Turtle, N-Triples, RDF/XML (powered by [oxrdf](https://docs.rs/oxrdf/)/[oxrdfio](https://docs.rs/oxrdfio/))
- Add JSON-LD context resolution with embedded RO-Crate 1.1/1.2 schema support
- Compaction: Contexts are used to compact expanded terms back to valid ROCrate 
- Testing: Add Python (rdflib) compatibility testing to verify semantic equivalence between Rust and Python RDF representations

Future implications: The full ROCrate expansion to RDF triples can be used to improve semantic validation of the ROCrate.

Completes: https://github.com/arunaengine/project-orga/issues/26

This requires the changes from: https://github.com/arunaengine/ro-crate-rs/pull/2 and should be rebased when this is merged.

author: cosmo83
body:
…ding

The Nimbus SDK's ClientSecretBasic implementation incorrectly URL-encodes special characters in client_id and client_secret before Base64 encoding them for HTTP Basic Authentication. This violates RFC 7617 and causes authentication failures with OAuth providers that use special characters in their credentials.

Example failure:
- Client ID: sb-app!t123
- Nimbus sends: Authorization: Basic Base64('sb-app%21t123:secret')
- Should send: Authorization: Basic Base64('sb-app!t123:secret')

This particularly affects SAP XSUAA and other OAuth providers that use special characters like '!', '$', '=' in their client credentials.

The fix replaces ClientSecretBasic with a custom implementation that correctly implements RFC 7617 by Base64 encoding the raw credentials without URL encoding.

Fixes: OAuth authentication with providers using special characters
